name: Clement Laurent
life: “I still remember washing my aunt's feet in the public showers.” Sunday often includes a stop at Juniper Street, where Clement knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I am an off-season local. I want the beach showers left open for those of us who still live here.
appearance: Clement has heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw. Look for auburn hair cut square at the nape. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a brown corduroy jacket with a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole. In conversation Clement grins on one side while the eyes stay serious.
personality: Clement finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To keep the showers available to residents.
family: Stella Rizzo is Clement’s second cousin. Clement brings the paper and a pen. Stella decides what stays off the paper. They have helped each other make decisions that were far easier to discuss once the figures could be moved around. The decisions themselves still belong to the person asking. Asked about *A tenant who stays*, Stella says, “I carried the saplings here for my cousin. I can identify which ones can travel.”
connections: Javier Rahman. The cart permit and the public showers are the two usable things that may outlast the season.
